reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should accept a string with semi colons

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should accept element handle as an argument

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should alias Window, Document and Node
reviewed.evidence: Evaluating '[window, document, document.body]' returns ['ref: <Window>', 'ref: <Document>', 'ref: <Node>'], so Page.evaluate's result serializer substitutes Playwright's ref aliases for host objects instead of failing or emptying them.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should await promise
reviewed.evidence: A callback returning Promise.resolve(8 * 7) resolves to 56, so Page.evaluate awaits a returned promise rather than serializing the promise object.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should await promise from popup
reviewed.evidence: The callback returns a promise built from another window's Promise constructor and Page.evaluate still resolves it to 42, so the await path does not depend on the promise coming from the document's own realm.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should evaluate date
reviewed.evidence: A returned { date: new Date('2020-05-27T01:31:38.506Z') } compares equal to the same Date, so Page.evaluate round-trips Date values instead of flattening them to strings.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should evaluate exception
reviewed.evidence: An Error returned by value keeps its message, its custom name 'foobar' and a stack naming innerFunction, so Page.evaluate serializes error objects with their own properties rather than as {}.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should evaluate exception with a function on the stack
reviewed.evidence: An Error created inside a named IIFE and returned by value keeps message 'error message' and a stack containing functionOnStack, so Page.evaluate preserves the stack captured in the document.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should evaluate in the page context
reviewed.evidence: After the fixture's native setup navigation to global-var.html, Page.evaluate('globalVar') returns 123, so the expression is evaluated against the document's own global scope. Page.goto is recorded as native fixture setup.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should evaluate url
reviewed.evidence: A returned { url: new URL('https://example.com') } compares equal to the same URL, so Page.evaluate round-trips URL values.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should ignore buggy toJSON
reviewed.evidence: Returned objects whose toJSON method and whose toJSON getter both throw serialize to {} instead of propagating those throws, so Page.evaluate's result serializer never invokes a page-supplied toJSON.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should modify global environment
reviewed.evidence: One Page.evaluate assigns window.globalVar = 123 and a later Page.evaluate('globalVar') reads back 123, so both calls run against the same document global scope.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should not add a toJSON property to newly created Arrays after evaluation
reviewed.evidence: After one Page.evaluate returns an array, a second one evaluates "'toJSON' in []" to false, so serializing an array result leaves no toJSON behind on Array.prototype.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should not expose the injected script export
reviewed.evidence: Page.evaluate('typeof pwExport === "undefined"') returns true, so evaluating a string expression sees the document's real globals and the adapter's bundled injected script left no pwExport there.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should not leak handles
reviewed.evidence: Page.evaluate('handles.length') rejects with a message containing ' handles', so the ReferenceError for the undeclared identifier reaches the caller instead of an internal handle table resolving it.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should not leak utility script
reviewed.evidence: Page.evaluate('this === window') returns true, so a string expression is evaluated with `this` bound to the document window rather than to an internal wrapper object.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should not use Array.prototype.toJSON when evaluating
reviewed.evidence: With Array.prototype.toJSON replaced by a function returning 'busted', the returned [1, 2, 3] still arrives as [1, 2, 3], so Page.evaluate ignores a page-defined Array toJSON.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should not use toJSON when evaluating
reviewed.evidence: A returned { toJSON: () => 'string', data: 'data' } arrives as { data: 'data', toJSON: {} }, so Page.evaluate serializes own properties instead of calling toJSON.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should properly serialize null arguments
reviewed.evidence: null passed as the argument is returned as null, so Page.evaluate does not collapse null into undefined or into a missing argument.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should properly serialize null fields
reviewed.evidence: A returned { a: null } keeps its null field, so Page.evaluate's result serializer preserves null values.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should properly serialize undefined arguments
reviewed.evidence: undefined passed as the argument and wrapped as { a: x } comes back as {}, so Page.evaluate drops an undefined field from the serialized result the way Playwright does.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should properly serialize undefined fields
reviewed.evidence: A returned { a: undefined } compares equal to {}, so undefined fields are dropped from the serialized value.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should properly serialize window.performance object
reviewed.evidence: The document's live window.performance is returned and matches the expected navigation and timing shape with numeric fields, so Page.evaluate serializes a host object into a plain structure rather than {}.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should reject promise with exception
reviewed.evidence: Reading a missing global in the callback rejects Page.evaluate with a message containing 'not_existing_object', so the in-document ReferenceError is surfaced to the caller.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should respect use strict expression
reviewed.evidence: A 'use strict' callback assigning an undeclared variableY rejects with a message containing 'variableY', so Page.evaluate keeps the callback's own strict-mode semantics.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should return -0
reviewed.evidence: Object.is(result, -0) holds for a returned -0, so the result serializer distinguishes -0 from 0.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should return -Infinity
reviewed.evidence: Object.is(result, -Infinity) holds for a returned -Infinity, so the result serializer carries it rather than null.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should return complex objects

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should return Infinity
reviewed.evidence: Object.is(result, Infinity) holds for a returned Infinity, so the result serializer carries it rather than null.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should return NaN
reviewed.evidence: Object.is(result, NaN) holds for a returned NaN, so the result serializer carries NaN rather than null.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should return undefined for non-serializable objects
reviewed.evidence: A callback returning a function yields undefined, so Page.evaluate drops a non-serializable result instead of rejecting.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should return undefined for objects with symbols
reviewed.evidence: Symbols as an array element, as an object key and nested inside an object serialize to [undefined], {} and { foo: [{ a: undefined }] }, so the result serializer drops symbol values and symbol-keyed properties.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should return undefined properties
reviewed.evidence: The value returned for { a: undefined } still reports "'a' in value" as true, so the key survives even though the value compares equal to {}.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should roundtrip promise to unserializable values
reviewed.evidence: A promise resolving to { infinity, nInfinity, nZero, nan } comes back with those exact values, so Page.evaluate awaits the promise and serializes the unserializable numbers inside it.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should roundtrip promise to value
reviewed.evidence: Promise.resolve(value) for null, Infinity, -0 and undefined resolves to each exact value, so Page.evaluate awaits the returned promise and preserves the identity of what it resolves with.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should roundtrip regex
reviewed.evidence: A RegExp passed as the argument and returned unchanged stringifies to /hello/im, so Page.evaluate carries RegExp arguments with their flags.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should roundtrip unserializable values
reviewed.evidence: An object of Infinity, -Infinity, -0 and NaN passed in and returned unchanged compares equal, so both the argument and the result serializer carry unserializable numbers.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should support thrown numbers as error messages
reviewed.evidence: A callback throwing the number 100500 rejects with a message containing '100500', so Page.evaluate reports non-Error throws instead of losing them.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should support thrown strings as error messages
reviewed.evidence: A callback throwing the string 'qwerty' rejects with a message containing 'qwerty', so Page.evaluate reports non-Error throws instead of losing them.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should throw error with detailed information on exception inside promise
reviewed.evidence: A throw inside the promise the callback returns rejects Page.evaluate with 'Error in promise', so a rejection of the awaited promise is reported rather than swallowed.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should transfer -0
reviewed.evidence: Object.is(result, -0) holds for -0 passed as the argument and echoed back, so the argument serializer distinguishes -0 from 0.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should transfer -Infinity
reviewed.evidence: -Infinity passed as the argument is echoed back identically, so the argument serializer carries it.

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should transfer NaN

reviewed.id: page-evaluate.spec.ts > should work for circular object
